_comment: SAMPLE DATA. Canned threat-workbench cell replies (persona-facing shape, threat-workbench-cell-persona.schema.json) for the hello-autotools fixture, extended from the replies used by appsec-review-process/tests/test_threat_workbench.py. pipeline/report/sample_data.py feeds them through threat_workbench.join and the overlay validator; no model was called.

pii-user-data-mapper.summary: One user-supplied value (the greeting name) enters through argv and is echoed to stdout and, with --report, into a JSON file.

data_classes.name: JSON greeting report
data_classes.retention_hint: kept until the user deletes the file

privacy_threats.statement: The --report option writes the user-supplied name to a JSON file whose permissions follow the process umask, so other local accounts may be able to read it.
proof_obligations: Show the mode the report file is created with and whether the path can be shared.
regulatory_candidate_notes: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) confidentiality may apply if the name is personal data (candidate)

notes.statement: The CLI runs as the invoking user on a single-user workstation.

deployment-topology-mapper.summary: Two declared zones: the Autotools build and the local shell that runs the binary.

abuse-scenario-analyst.summary: A local user controls argv and the --report path.

abuse_scenarios.attacker_objective: Corrupt memory through an oversized greeting name
preconditions: the binary is invoked with an attacker-chosen name

attack-tree-builder.summary: One tree for the memory-corruption objective.

attack_trees.objective: Corrupt memory through the greeting formatter

nodes.label: supply a name longer than the buffer

supply-chain-specialist.summary: Vendored cJSON 1.7.18 is compiled into hello from in-tree source and has no package identity in the SBOM.

abuse_scenarios.attacker_objective: Get modified cJSON code into the hello binary
abuse_scenarios.actor: contributor or upstream source with write access to vendor/
abuse_scenarios.capability: changes the vendored cJSON sources before a build
abuse_scenarios.harm: attacker-chosen code runs inside hello and can alter or leak the JSON report
preconditions: the vendored copy is refreshed or edited without a comparison against the upstream release
missing_controls: checksum or signature pin for vendor/cJSON-1.7.18
purl or CPE for the vendored copy in the SBOM

attack_trees.objective: Get modified cJSON code into the hello binary

nodes.label: modified cJSON is linked into hello
a maintainer copies a tampered upstream release into vendor/
the build compiles vendor/ sources into libcjson.a

gaps.statement: Vendored cJSON 1.7.18 carries no purl or CPE, so advisory matching could not cover it.
